record.original_question: Does the mapping class group of a closed surface have a nontrivial Schreier growth gap, that is, must every faithful action of that group on a set X have Vol_{G,X}(n) bounded below by some superlinear function up to the paper's asymptotic comparison?

evidence.quote: Definition 6.1. We say that G has Schreier growth gap f if for every faithful action of G on a set X we have Vol_{G,X}(n) succcurlyeq f(n). The gap is said to be nontrivial if f is superlinear.
Question 6.4. Does the mapping class group of a closed surface have nontrivial Schreier growth gap?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a group acting on a set $X$. Fix a finite generating set $S$ of $G$ and, for $x\in X$, let $B_{G,X}(n,x)$ denote the set of points of $X$ reachable from $x$ by a word of length at most $n$ in $S\cup S^{-1}$. Define the volume function
$$\mathrm{Vol}_{G,X}(n)=\sup_{x\in X}|B_{G,X}(n,x)|,$$
which depends on $S$ only up to the usual asymptotic equivalence $f\preccurlyeq g \iff \exists C>0: f(n)\le Cg(Cn)$ for all large $n$.

Say that $G$ has Schreier growth gap $f$ if for every faithful action of $G$ on a set $X$ one has $\mathrm{Vol}_{G,X}(n)\succcurlyeq f(n)$. The gap is called nontrivial if $f$ is superlinear (i.e. $f(n)/n\to\infty$).

Question: Let $\Sigma$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $g\ge 2$ and let $G=\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma)$ be its mapping class group. Does $G$ admit a nontrivial Schreier growth gap?
artifact.category_tag: Mapping class groups and growth of group actions
artifact.status_search_result: The notion of Schreier growth gap was introduced in recent work on growth of group actions, where nontrivial gaps were established for various classes of solvable groups. No source found establishes or refutes a nontrivial Schreier growth gap for mapping class groups of closed surfaces; the question is posed as an open problem and no resolution appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Growth of actions of solvable groups
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces Schreier growth gap and proves results for solvable (in particular metabelian) groups; no result for mapping class groups is given.
status_evidence.claim: The Schreier growth gap framework is developed and applied to solvable groups, leaving the mapping class group case as a question.
